metric: functional one-bit primitive operations per second
landauer_formula: eta_L = bitops_per_second * k_B * T * ln(2) / associated_power_watts

1940.note: Late relay/electromechanical tabulation and special-purpose wartime machines; deliberately very broad.

1945.note: Colossus/ENIAC-era one-off electronic machines on top of relay and punched-card computation; geometric mean of neighbours.

1950.note: A handful-to-dozens of large electronic machines plus relay/electromechanical computing.

1960.note: Commercial mainframes, SAGE-scale military systems, early transistor machines.

1970.note: Mainframes plus rapidly expanding minicomputers and embedded control.

1980.note: Mainframes/minicomputers plus early personal computers, consoles, calculators, and embedded microprocessors.

1990.source_class: Hilbert/Lopez-interpolated capacity converted to actual bitops
1990.note: Interpolated between 1986 and 1993 global MIPS capacity anchors, then converted to realized functional bitops.

1995.source_class: Hilbert/Lopez-interpolated capacity converted to actual bitops
1995.note: Interpolated between 1993 and 2000 global MIPS capacity anchors; web/PC expansion era.

2000.source_class: Hilbert/Lopez capacity + Koomey data-centre power anchor
2000.note: PC peak in general-purpose capacity; data-centre wall power anchored near 70.8 TWh/year plus end-user/embedded/networking.

2005.source_class: Hilbert/Lopez capacity + Koomey data-centre power anchor
2005.note: Fast GPU/application-specific growth; data-centre wall power anchored near 152.5 TWh/year plus network/end-user/embedded.

2010.note: Smartphone and cloud era; data centres anchored near 194 TWh/year.

2015.note: Cloud, mobile, consoles, conventional accelerators; data centres and transmission networks roughly 200 and 220 TWh/year respectively.

2020.note: Pre-generative-AI but GPU/TPU usage is material; data centres near low-200 TWh/year and networks rising.

2025.note: AI-accelerator ramp year; IEA puts data centres at ~485 TWh (AI-focused ~155 TWh) in 2025.

2026.source_class: current-day anchor from detailed 2026 point estimate
2026.note: Current non-PoW artificial computation; dominated by AI accelerators, with conventional data centres, networks, PCs, phones and embedded devices as secondary contributors.

2015.note: ASIC-era Bitcoin mining; other SHA-256 PoW is small but not forced to zero.

2020.note: Large-scale ASIC mining; hash-rate and fleet efficiency dominate the inclusive estimate.

2026.note: Near-zettahash/s SHA-256 PoW (about 1.0 ZH/s 7-day average, Oct 2026); fleet efficiency ~20-21.5 J/TH (J.P. Morgan).

2025.note: 2025 average hashrate ~0.8-1.09 ZH/s; fleet efficiency ~21.5-22 J/TH (J.P. Morgan Q2-Q3 2025).
